what_it_does: This paper studies how unpredictable system noise (operating system scheduling delays, shared cache interference, NUMA memory effects) corrupts the measured performance of parallel applications, making benchmarking unreliable and inconsistent. The researchers build a framework to capture traces of real system noise and replay it back during experiments as controlled perturbations. They then evaluate two parallel programming models—OpenMP and SYCL—under both noisy and clean conditions, testing mitigation strategies like pinning threads to specific cores, isolating certain cores for system tasks, and toggling simultaneous multithreading on and off to see what reduces noise's impact.
